stubs.angle: Given a Grid with RowDefinitions="Auto,*,Auto", which row gets the remaining height of the page?
stubs.answerHinge: An Auto row is sized to its content, while a star row shares the space left after Auto and absolute rows, so the middle star row takes the remaining height.

stubs.angle: What must you do before Shell.Current.GoToAsync("orderdetails") can open a detail page that is not declared in AppShell.xaml?
stubs.answerHinge: A page outside the Shell visual hierarchy must be registered with Routing.RegisterRoute before you navigate to it. Without that registration, navigation to the route fails.

stubs.angle: Where should a .NET MAUI app store a user's refresh token: Preferences, SecureStorage, a file in AppDataDirectory, or a static field?
stubs.answerHinge: SecureStorage encrypts values with the platform key stores (Keychain, Android Keystore-backed storage, Windows DataProtection), while Preferences keeps plain text.

stubs.angle: What execution states does a .NET MAUI app go through, and which Window events are raised on each transition?
stubs.answerHinge: An app moves between not running, running, deactivated and stopped. The Window raises Created, Activated, Deactivated, Stopped, Resumed and Destroying as it crosses those states.

stubs.angle: Why does VerticalOptions="End" on a button inside a page-filling VerticalStackLayout not move the button to the bottom of the screen, and what fixes it?
stubs.answerHinge: A stack layout gives each child only the size it asks for in the stacking direction, so vertical alignment has no extra space to work with. A Grid with a star row, or placing the button in its own Auto row, moves it to the bottom.

stubs.angle: Which of Entry.Text, Slider.Value, Switch.IsToggled and Label.Text bind TwoWay by default when no Mode is given?
stubs.answerHinge: Each bindable property declares its own default binding mode: user-editable properties such as Entry.Text, Slider.Value and Switch.IsToggled default to TwoWay, while Label.Text defaults to OneWay.

stubs.angle: In a view model that uses CommunityToolkit.Mvvm with a field-based [ObservableProperty] counter, find the line that keeps the label from updating after a command runs.
stubs.answerHinge: The generator raises PropertyChanged only from the generated property setter, so writing the backing field directly (_count++) changes the value without notifying the binding.

stubs.angle: What is the recommended way to pass an Order object (not just its id) to a detail page with Shell navigation?
stubs.answerHinge: Pass the object in an IDictionary<string, object> navigation parameter of GoToAsync, and receive it with IQueryAttributable.ApplyQueryAttributes or QueryProperty. Query-string parameters carry only strings.

stubs.angle: A view model loads orders with await ... .ConfigureAwait(false) and then adds them to an ObservableCollection bound to a CollectionView, and the app crashes on Android. Find the line with the defect.
stubs.answerHinge: After ConfigureAwait(false) the continuation runs on a thread-pool thread, and changing a collection bound to native UI off the main thread is not allowed. Marshal the change with MainThread.BeginInvokeOnMainThread, or keep the continuation on the UI context.

stubs.angle: How do you get view models and services injected into page constructors in .NET MAUI, and which lifetime should pages and view models get?
stubs.answerHinge: Register pages, view models and services in MauiProgram.CreateMauiApp. Shell then resolves registered page types through the container when it navigates to a route. Transient pages and view models avoid stale state between visits, while a singleton keeps one instance for the whole app.

stubs.angle: How do #if ANDROID / #if IOS blocks compare with partial classes in the Platforms folders for platform-specific code in a single MAUI project, and when do you choose each?
stubs.answerHinge: Conditional compilation suits a few lines but scatters platform branches through shared code. Partial classes with per-platform files keep one shared API with separate implementations, and the build compiles only the files for the target platform.

stubs.angle: Where should a page start loading its data: the constructor, OnAppearing or OnNavigatedTo, and what changes when the user comes back to the page from a detail page?
stubs.answerHinge: The constructor runs once per page instance, while OnAppearing runs every time the page becomes visible again, including on back navigation. Loading there repeats the work unless the code guards it or refreshes on purpose.

stubs.angle: Which statements about the Shell route forms "//orders", "..", "../details" and "details" are true?
stubs.answerHinge: "//" navigates to an absolute route in the Shell hierarchy and replaces the navigation stack, ".." pops one page, "../details" pops and then pushes, and a relative route pushes onto the current stack.

stubs.angle: An editor screen must not lose an unsaved draft when the OS kills the app in the background. Which Window event is the reliable place to persist it?
stubs.answerHinge: Once an app is stopped (in the background), the OS may terminate its process without raising Destroying, so the draft must be saved in Stopped (or earlier, in Deactivated), not in Destroying.

stubs.angle: How does WeakReferenceMessenger differ from StrongReferenceMessenger in CommunityToolkit.Mvvm when a page's view model registers for messages and the page is closed?
stubs.answerHinge: WeakReferenceMessenger holds recipients through weak references, so a view model that was never unregistered can still be collected. StrongReferenceMessenger keeps it alive until it is unregistered explicitly.

stubs.angle: Code that removes the Android underline from a custom BorderlessEntry through EntryHandler.Mapper.AppendToMapping removes it from every Entry in the app. Find the line with the defect.
stubs.answerHinge: Handler mapper changes are global for every instance of the control type, so the mapping action must check that the view is a BorderlessEntry before changing the native control.

stubs.angle: Bindings work in Debug but some fields stay empty in a trimmed Release build for iOS. Why does this happen, and how do you fix it without turning trimming off?
stubs.answerHinge: Reflection-based bindings reach properties only by name, so the trimmer cannot see that those members are used and may remove them. Compiled bindings with x:DataType create static references that the trimmer keeps, and trimmer warnings show the remaining reflection uses.

stubs.angle: When does Shell fit a MAUI app better than a NavigationPage-based navigation stack, and what does Shell constrain?
stubs.answerHinge: Shell gives URI-based routing, flyout and tab structure, and page resolution through DI, but it imposes a fixed visual hierarchy. NavigationPage offers manual push and pop stacks without routes, and the two models are not meant to be nested together.

stubs.angle: Which practices reduce measure and arrange cost of a complex MAUI page?
stubs.answerHinge: Each nested layout adds its own measure and arrange passes, so replacing nested StackLayouts with one Grid, removing layouts that hold a single child and avoiding unneeded Auto sizing cut layout work. Adding more wrapper layouts does not.

stubs.angle: App memory grows by several megabytes every time a user opens and closes an order detail page. How do you find what keeps the page alive?
stubs.answerHinge: First prove that the popped page is not collected (a WeakReference check after a forced GC, or dotnet-gcdump from the device). Then trace its root, typically a subscription to a long-lived service or messenger, a singleton-registered page or view model, or a platform cycle in a custom handler.

stubs.angle: A CollectionView with 5,000 product rows stutters while scrolling on mid-range Android phones. What do you check and change?
stubs.answerHinge: Virtualization depends on a parent that constrains the CollectionView's size (not a ScrollView or StackLayout). Then lighten the item template, size and cache images, and set ItemSizingStrategy=MeasureFirstItem when rows share one height, so items are not each measured.

stubs.angle: Your team owns a large Xamarin.Forms app with many custom renderers and third-party controls, and Xamarin support ended on May 1, 2024. How do you plan the move to .NET MAUI?
stubs.answerHinge: Inventory the blockers first (third-party packages without MAUI versions, custom renderers, platform effects). Migrate with renderers shimmed where possible, then convert them to handlers step by step, so each step ships instead of one long freeze.

stubs.angle: How do you decide between hand-written INotifyPropertyChanged base classes, CommunityToolkit.Mvvm and a full framework such as Prism for a team starting a MAUI app?
stubs.answerHinge: The choice weighs boilerplate saved, team familiarity and how much the library dictates navigation and structure against dependency risk and upgrade cost. A toolkit of generators keeps view models plain, while a framework standardizes more but couples the app to its release cycle.

stubs.angle: What team rules do you set for requesting runtime permissions such as location or camera in a MAUI app so the behaviour is consistent across Android and iOS?
stubs.answerHinge: Permissions are checked with Permissions.CheckStatusAsync and requested with RequestAsync at the point of use on the main thread, behind one shared service that also handles the denied state with an explanation, because each platform declares permissions differently and a denied request may not show the prompt again.

stubs.angle: Which team rules keep MAUI view models unit-testable without a device or emulator?
stubs.answerHinge: View models stay testable when they do not reference Microsoft.Maui.Controls types and reach navigation, dialogs and the main thread through injected abstractions. Calling Shell.Current or Application.Current directly from a view model ties it to a running UI.

stubs.angle: How do you design an offline-first MAUI client that syncs with backend services for years while old app versions stay installed on users' devices?
stubs.answerHinge: The device keeps a local store (for example SQLite) and a queue of pending changes that a sync protocol replays with conflict rules. Because users update apps late, the backend must accept the sync contracts of several app versions at once and retire them by an explicit policy.

stubs.angle: A company has a Blazor web app and plans mobile and desktop clients. Leadership asks whether to share the UI through MAUI Blazor Hybrid or build native XAML clients. What do you recommend and why?
stubs.answerHinge: Blazor Hybrid runs Razor components from a shared class library natively in a BlazorWebView and reaches device APIs through .NET, which maximizes reuse with the web app. XAML clients give a native look and finer platform control, so the decision depends on how much of the product needs native-feeling UI and per-platform features.
